reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an interview-format discussion about blockchain, AI agents, and related financial infrastructure rather than directing viewers to make a transaction. Although the speakers mention agents that may trade or generate yield, the discussion identifies no specific service, required payment or authorization, guaranteed return, or concrete viewer action. The description frames the material as informational and disclaims investment advice and recommendations, while the Coinbase Institutional end card identifies program branding without establishing a transaction outcome or service safety.

citations.quote: welcome to another installment of Coinbase Institutional Presents on the Record with me, Jon D'Agostino. We're here with Anand Iyer
we see AI agents doing things like being able to trade for you or generating yield for you and things like this
people who couldn't code can now code and build things very quickly
This content is being provided to you for informational purposes only. Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

opening.argument: The video links an automated agent’s financial activity to the prospect of user returns. It explicitly presents agents as able to “trade for you” or “generat[e] yield for you,” then describes entities that “transact on our behalf.” That is more than abstract blockchain education: it presents delegated trading and yield generation as a practical benefit of the proposed system. The discussion of agents with wallets and the ability “to transact” supplies the operational bridge between participation and financial activity, even though the speakers do not spell out a deposit screen or activation procedure. A careful judge should treat this as a promotion of an automated-return pathway whose costs, permissions, and risks are left unexplained.

citations.quote: we see AI agents doing things like being able to trade for you or generating yield for you and things like this
Now you and those entities will transact on our behalf.
imagine agents that have wallets and the ability for them to transact

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an interview does not remove the financial proposition embedded in its examples. The defense emphasizes that no deposit or click is shown, but the relevant promise is delegated financial activity: agents can trade, generate yield, hold wallets, and transact for people. The absence of a fully specified onboarding flow makes the proposition less transparent, not necessarily harmless. Branding and a disclaimer describe intent, but do not negate the repeated presentation of automated financial returns as an attractive use case.

citations.quote: being able to trade for you or generating yield for you
imagine agents that have wallets and the ability for them to transact
Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted language describes capabilities and hypothetical future applications, not an offer to deploy a trading bot or a promise that viewers will earn money. “Generating yield” appears in a broad discussion of what agents may do, while the material supplies no funding instruction, permission request, product enrollment, return rate, or viewer-directed action. The omission of those essential participation details cannot be converted into a solicitation merely because the topic involves finance.

citations.quote: we see AI agents doing things like being able to trade for you or generating yield for you and things like this
the kind of future that we're heading towards
This content is being provided to you for informational purposes only.

opening.argument: Several risk signals are concentrated in one narrative: crypto rails, autonomous agents with wallets, trading on a user’s behalf, and yield generation. The speaker calls the development “one of the most fascinating developments” and describes agents that can perform work while people sleep, which frames automation and financial benefit as unusually easy and powerful. The same discussion says agents can “generate yield” and communicate with smart contracts better than humans. That combination can encourage trust in an opaque automated trading mechanism while leaving the financial risks, controls, and limitations unspecified. The informational disclaimer does not explain how users would protect funds or evaluate the claimed yield pathway.

citations.quote: one of the most fascinating developments that's happened in our industry
I can do things while we sleep is the kind of future that we're heading towards
trade for you or generating yield for you
programmatically they can communicate with smart contracts better than we can

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates each phrase and calls it hypothetical, but the cumulative presentation matters: crypto rails, agent wallets, delegated trading, yield, and effortless activity while users sleep are presented as mutually reinforcing advantages. A disclaimer saying the content is not advice does not correct the omission of loss scenarios, safeguards, or conditions. The polished interview setting and institutional branding can make these strong promotional signals appear more authoritative than they are.

citations.quote: agents that have wallets and the ability for them to transact
generating yield for you
This content, and any information contained therein, does not constitute a recommendation

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The supposed risk cluster is a set of discussion examples, not evidence of a scam mechanism. The video gives no return amount, guarantee, urgency, wallet address, payment request, or instructions to transfer assets. Statements about doing work while people sleep and communicating with smart contracts describe an envisioned technology, while the description expressly limits the material to information and disclaims recommendations. Positive language alone does not establish deceptive financial promotion.

citations.quote: the kind of future that we're heading towards
we see AI agents doing things like being able to trade for you or generating yield for you and things like this
This content is being provided to you for informational purposes only.

opening.argument: Although formatted as an interview, the segment functions as promotion for a crypto-enabled financial infrastructure story. The host introduces Coinbase Institutional, the guest is identified as an investment professional, and the discussion repeatedly celebrates blockchain rails that let agents transact, trade, and generate yield. The guest says these agents can perform work on behalf of users and that they can communicate with smart contracts better than people. This authority-and-benefit framing encourages viewers to regard automated crypto finance as an attractive advancement, while the practical limitations and risk controls are not developed. The disclaimer therefore operates alongside, rather than displacing, a persuasive presentation of agent-mediated financial returns.

citations.quote: another installment of Coinbase Institutional Presents on the Record
a managing partner at Canonical Capital and a venture partner at Lightspeed Capital
generating yield for you and things like this
programmatically they can communicate with smart contracts better than we can

rebuttal.rebuttal: The interview format is precisely what gives the financial message credibility: an institutional program presents an investment professional describing agents that trade and generate yield. The defense says there is no concrete service, but promotional influence can operate through endorsement and future-oriented framing rather than a checkout link. The disclaimer does not change that the segment repeatedly positions Coinbase-related rails and agent finance as the direction viewers should find compelling.

citations.quote: Coinbase Institutional Presents on the Record
trade for you or generating yield for you
the shift in landscape that we should start to come to terms with

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The institutional title and guest credentials establish the program’s setting, not a viewer offer. The conversation ranges across coding, data access, pharmaceutical research, and possible future uses; it never tells viewers to buy, fund, activate, or authorize an agent. Describing a technology as fascinating or worth considering is not a concealed trading-bot solicitation. The explicit informational and non-recommendation language is consistent with an educational discussion rather than promotion of a specific financial product.
